source_text: Sed quae in perditionem non processu liberae voluntatis, verum informatoris sui potestate cogantur.
pass_a_gloss: But which are compelled into perdition not by the process of a free will, but by the power of their own former.

lemmas.lexica: LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS liber=free; also children; context decides

pass_b_english: But vessels driven to destruction not by the course of their free will but by the power of their maker.

choices.why: Freedom to abstain is required for will and sin.
Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: Continues the preceding sentence about vessels destined for destruction.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
